title: Vila Marebo / Frederico Zanelato | Arquitetos
text:
Vila Marebo / Frederico Zanelato | Arquitetos

The design of Vila Marebo, in southern Bahia, was born from the invitation of a long-time partner. The premise was clear: to create two independent blocks connected by a footbridge and a generous pergola. More than a residence, the proposal was to conceive a true village that embraces the lot. This fluid zoning encourages encounters, conversations, and leisure, transforming the pathways and surrounding spaces into environments of pure warmth and sensory experience.

title: casa POP / gon architects
text:
casa POP / gon architects

Casa POP is based on the premise that there is no such thing as a standard user, and therefore architecture must adapt to unique ways of living. The original home, a 78 m² apartment located in Vicálvaro, was built in the 2000s under the rigid standards of the traditional nuclear family, resulting in a highly compartmentalized layout full of hallways. This distribution was obsolete for its owners, Santiago and Ángel, a couple whose lives revolve around enjoyment, knowledge, and culture.

title: Imbriani – Renovation of Two Apartments in Milan / co.arch studio
text:
Imbriani – Renovation of Two Apartments in Milan / co.arch studio

The project transforms two small early 20th-century apartments in Milan's Bovisa district, organized around a shared threshold. This threshold became the conceptual starting point of the intervention: a spatial device that separates and connects two distinct domestic identities, expressed immediately through two contrasting chromatic atmospheres—terra red and matcha green.

title: Between Burning Forests and Utopian Cities: Designing the Climate Transition
text:
Between Burning Forests and Utopian Cities: Designing the Climate Transition

There is no shortage of ways to imagine what the world will look like after a climate catastrophe. Genres of movies and novels have been built around the question of what happens when contemporary safeguards fail, from dystopian fiction and post-apocalyptic literature to disaster films, graphic novels, and video games. Burning forests, submerged cities, abandoned infrastructure, resource scarcity, and mass displacement are a familiar visual and narrative vocabulary. We have become remarkably fluent in imagining the consequences of a world that fails to respond to climate change.

title: Cabins at the Tip, Sunny Lakes, Senec / ER Atelier
text:
Cabins at the Tip, Sunny Lakes, Senec / ER Atelier

The project of two recreational buildings at the tip of Sunny Lakes in Senec approaches two separate structures as a single architectural and landscape composition. Located on a prominent waterfront peninsula, the site is characterized by an unregulated mixture of recreational buildings from different periods and architectural styles. Rather than introducing another isolated expression, the proposal seeks to redefine the entire tip through a unified architectural language, while preserving the memory of the site and strengthening its relationship with the lake and the public realm.

title: The Full Moon / SHISUO design office
text:
The Full Moon / SHISUO design office

Invited by the Power Station of Art (PSA), SHISUO Design Office has unveiled "The Full Moon" an urban public art installation celebrating the Mid-Autumn Festival in Shanghai. The installation was realized in collaboration with Shi Qinling, a Shanghai-style paper-cutting inheritor, and is themed around the moon, rabbits, and the art of paper-cutting. Across various cultures, the rabbit holds a unique place in the human imagination as one of the few animal figures beloved by all. In China's classical Mid-Autumn folklore, the rabbit is a constant companion to the moon—the moon symbolizes the cyclical waxing and waning of existence, while the rabbit metaphorically represents the vitality, growth, and flourishing of all beings.

title: PH Olaguer / CDC ARQ
text:
PH Olaguer / CDC ARQ

Rather than adding elements, the project proposes concentrating functions to free up space. Spatial continuity, the connection to the courtyard, and a single, continuous piece of millwork that guides the journey create a small yet spatially generous home, where architecture serves as a tool for spatial organization.

title: Residência em Campos do Jordão / Gil Mello Arquitetura
text:
Residência em Campos do Jordão / Gil Mello Arquitetura

The presented project is the result of a complete renovation, based on the premise of reusing the existing perimeter walls, foundations and slabs. This design strategy aimed to optimize resources and execution time, made possible by a feasibility study that confirmed the capacity of the existing structure to accommodate the new program of needs.

title: Villas Raices / Vince Studio
text:
Villas Raices / Vince Studio

Villas Raíces was born from the intention of inhabiting the mountain with the least possible impact, allowing the architecture to adapt to the terrain and not the other way around.

title: Jeronimo Faria Lima Building / Perkins&Will São Paulo
text:
Jeronimo Faria Lima Building / Perkins&Will São Paulo

At one of São Paulo’s most emblematic corners—where the intensity of Brigadeiro Faria Lima Avenue meets the walkable scale of Jeronimo da Veiga Street—Jeronimo Faria Lima does not seek to assert itself through height, form, or presence in the skyline alone. The project is guided by a deeper ambition: to make the encounter between architecture and the city a fundamental part of the experience.

title: Panorama House / Studio B Architecture + Interiors
text:
Panorama House / Studio B Architecture + Interiors

The Panorama House project involved both renovating and expanding an existing residence originally designed by the renowned mid-century architect, James Hunter. The structure's distinguished heritage and the innovative architectural solution garnered it recognition as a Historic Landmark during the rigorous approval process. Designed for homeowners seeking a peaceful retreat, the residence carefully balances privacy amidst cherished landmarks and bustling trails while embracing the natural beauty of its surroundings.

title: Space Architecture Week
text:
Space Architecture Week

During World Space Week, architecture expands its boundaries. The new space race raises a fundamental question for today's designers: how do we imagine, build, and inhabit beyond Earth?

From October 5 to 8, 2026, the Faculty of Architecture, Design and Urbanism at the University of Buenos Aires will host Space Architecture Week, a Latin American gathering that will bring together architecture, science, technology, and design.

Through workshops, a space architecture hackathon, international guests, talks, interviews, and exhibitions, students, professionals, and specialists will explore new ways to inhabit the Moon, Mars, and other environments.

title: Launch of the Glossary for the City of Our Future
text:
Launch of the Glossary for the City of Our Future

Glossary for the City of Our Future Gathers Experts to Reflect on the Cities of Tomorrow with Hope

What kind of city do we want to build for future generations? This is the central question of Glossary for the City of Our Future with Hope, a book organized and edited by architect and professor Thereza Christina Couto Carvalho. The launch will take place on September 28 at 6:30 PM at Livraria da Travessa in Ipanema, Rio de Janeiro.

Published by Rio Books, the book brings together 47 contributors—including researchers, architects, urban planners, and experts from various fields—to offer an interdisciplinary reflection on contemporary challenges.

text:

This University of Porto conference marks the 55th anniversary of the UNESCO World Heritage Convention. It explores heritage across art, architecture, history, museums, digital culture, tourism, sustainability and communities, making it fully interdisciplinary.

Taking place in Porto, it is held in a city that characterizes the issues at play: a coastal city, a historic maritime centre and Europe’s first protected wine region. Its core is a World Heritage Site and a National Monument of Portugal.

From this unique setting, the conference considers questions of heritage globally.

Tallinn Design Festival / Disainiöö returns from 28 September to 4 October 2026 for its 21st edition, bringing together contemporary Estonian design, international designers, exhibitions, talks, installations, workshops and city-wide events.

Taking place primarily at Põhjala Factory, a former industrial complex in northern Tallinn, this year’s festival focuses on the theme “Future of Product Design”.

title: The Lives of Ephemeral Form
text:
The Lives of Ephemeral Form

The Lives of Ephemeral Form examines how architecture persists, changes, and disappears through its records, and what happens when those records are themselves unstable.

Developed as part of the Architectural Institute of Japan’s 140th anniversary program, the exhibition is the first phase of a two-year project devoted to the act of documentation. It brings together installations, archival research, photography, moving images, screenings, talks, guided programs, and work carried out publicly in the gallery.

Architecture is often associated with permanence. Yet buildings depend on unstable conditions: economic circumstances, technologies, changing patterns of use, material resources, and the less visible forces that transform cities.

title: Light Through the Wall: Indian House Interiors Shaped by Brick Jali
text:
Light Through the Wall: Indian House Interiors Shaped by Brick Jali

A brick façade does more than define the façade of a house. When designed as a porous screen, it becomes an intermediary between inside and outside, shaping the atmosphere and environmental conditions of the spaces behind it. Across contemporary Indian residential architecture, brick jali — a perforated or lattice brick screen — has been reinterpreted with a contemporary sensibility, drawing on vernacular architectural elements.
